steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The practical component is worth 60% of the total GCSE — performance and choreography combined

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Performance (30%) includes one solo and one duet/trio performance of set phrases

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Choreography (30%) requires a solo or group choreography in response to a chosen stimulus

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Performance marks reward technical accuracy, physical skills, expressive skills and mental skills

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What are the four categories of performance skills assessed in AQA 8236? | Q: Why is it important to rehearse under exam conditions? | Q: What should you include in your programme note?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Technical accuracy, physical skills (flexibility, strength, stamina), expressive skills (projection, musicality, focus) and mental skills (commitment, concentration, confidence, responsiveness). | Rehearsing under exam conditions builds familiarity with the performance environment, reduces anxiety, and ensures you can perform at your best without the support of mirrors or teacher prompts. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Warm up thoroughly before performing — physical and vocal preparation prevents injury and focuses the mind Perform to the back row of the audience space — project your energy and intention beyond the examiner If you make a mistake, keep going without stopping — continuity and commitment are assessed Write your programme note early and refine it — it is assessed alongside the choreography Practise your choreography in different spaces so you can adapt to the exam room on the day
